passages.text: The following MD&A is intended to assist the reader in understanding Amgen’s business. MD&A is provided as a supplement to, and should be read in conjunction with, our consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes. Our results of operations discussed in MD&A are presented in conformity with GAAP. Amgen operates in one operating segment: human therapeutics. Therefore, our results of operations are discussed on a consolidated basis. Forward-looking statements This report and other documents we file with the SEC contain forward-looking statements that are based on current expectations, estimates, forecasts and projections about us, our future performance, our business, our beliefs and our management’s assumptions. In addition, we, or others on our behalf, may make forward-looking statements in press releases, written statements or our communications and discussions with investors and analysts in the normal course of business through meetings, webcasts, phone calls and conference calls. Such words as “expect,” “anticipate,” “outlook,” “could,” “target,” “project,” “intend,” “plan,” “believe,” “seek,” “estimate,” “should,” “may,” “assume” and “continue” as well as variations of such words and similar expressions are intended to identify such forward-looking statements. These statements are not guarantees of future performance and they involve certain risks, uncertainties and assumptions that are difficult to predict. We describe our respective risks, uncertainties and assumptions that could affect the outcome or results of operations in Part I, Item 1A. Risk Factors. We have based our forward-looking statements on our management’s beliefs and assumptions based on information available to our management at the time the statements are made. We caution you that actual outcomes and results may differ materially from what is expressed, implied or forecasted by our forward-looking statements. Reference is made in particular to forward-looking statements regarding product sales, regulatory activities, clinical trial results, reimbursement, expenses, EPS, liquidity and capital resources, trends, planned dividends, stock repurchases and collaborations. Except as required under the federal securities laws and the rules and regulations of the SEC, we do not have any intention or obligation to update publicly any forward-looking statements after the distribution of this report, whether as a result of new information, future events, changes in assumptions or otherwise. Overview Amgen Inc. (including its subsidiaries, referred to as “Amgen,” “the Company,” “we,” “our” or “us”) discovers, develops, manufactures and delivers innovative medicines to fight some of the world’s toughest diseases. We focus on areas of high unmet medical need and leverage our expertise to strive for solutions that dramatically improve people’s lives, while also reducing the social and economic burden of disease. We helped launch the biotechnology industry more than 45 years ago and have grown to be one of the world’s leading independent biotechnology companies. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: This report and other documents we file with the SEC contain forward-looking statements that are based on current expectations, estimates, forecasts and projections about us, our future performance, our business, our beliefs and our management’s assumptions. These statements are not guarantees of future performance and involve certain risks, uncertainties and assumptions that are difficult to predict. You should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties our business faces. The risks described below are not the only ones we face. Our business is also subject to the risks that affect many other companies, such as employment relations, general economic conditions, geopolitical events and international operations. Further, additional risks not currently known to us or that we currently believe are immaterial may in the future materially and adversely affect our business, operations, liquidity and stock price. SUMMARY Risks Related to Government Regulations and Third-Party Policies • Our sales depend on coverage and reimbursement from government and commercial third-party payers, and pricing and reimbursement pressures have affected, and are likely to continue to affect, our profitability. • Guidelines and recommendations published by various organizations can reduce the use of our products. • We could be subject to additional tax liabilities, including from an adverse outcome in our ongoing tax dispute with the IRS and other tax examinations, enactment of the OECD minimum corporate tax rate agreement and the adoption and interpretation of new tax legislation, including OB3. Such tax liabilities could adversely affect our profitability and results of operations. • Our business may be affected by litigation and government investigations. Risks Related to Economic Conditions and Operating a Global Business • Our efforts to collaborate with or acquire other companies, products, or technology, and to integrate the operations of companies or to support the products or technology we have acquired, may not be successful, and may result in unanticipated costs, delays or failures to realize the benefits of the transactions. • A breakdown of our information technology systems, cyberattack or information security breach could significantly compromise the confidentiality, integrity and availability of our information technology systems, network-connected control systems and/or our data, interrupt the operation of our business and/or affect our reputation. • Our sales and operations are subject to the risks of doing business internationally, including in new or emerging markets. • We may not be able to access the capital and credit markets on terms that are favorable to us, or at all. credit_strengths.text: Amgen's revenue base is substantial and growing, with annual sales exceeding thirty-six billion. The company's operating margin is roughly twenty-five percent, well above the health care sector median, reflecting strong pricing power and cost discipline. This profitability supports internal cash generation and provides a buffer against margin pressure from biosimilar competition and reimbursement headwinds.

Operating cash flow remains robust at nearly ten billion, comfortably covering capital expenditures and generating free cash flow of over eight billion. This cash generation underpins the company's ability to service debt, fund dividends, and invest in its pipeline. The consistent cash flow also provides flexibility to manage upcoming maturities without relying on external financing.

key_risks.text: Amgen faces significant pricing and reimbursement pressures from government and commercial payers, as highlighted in the risk factors. These pressures could erode revenue and profitability, especially as biosimilar competition intensifies. Additionally, an ongoing tax dispute with the IRS and potential changes from OECD minimum tax rules could result in additional liabilities, further straining cash flows.

The debt maturity profile shows a substantial portion due after year five, but near-term maturities include a notable amount in the next twelve months. With cash balances covering only a portion of these obligations, the company will need to refinance or use operating cash flow. Any disruption in credit markets could increase refinancing costs or strain liquidity.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage stands at approximately three and a third times, below the sector median, indicating that operating income covers interest expense but with less cushion than peers. This relatively tight coverage, combined with significant leverage, suggests that debt servicing is manageable but vulnerable to earnings declines. A drop in operating income could quickly pressure coverage ratios.

Free cash flow to debt is modest at under fifteen percent, and the ratio of operating cash flow to debt is also below sector norms. This indicates that internal cash generation, while positive, does not rapidly deleverage the balance sheet. The company relies on consistent cash flows to service debt, and any operational setback could impair its ability to reduce leverage organically.

overall_credit_view.text: Amgen's credit profile is characterized by significant leverage, with net debt to EBITDA above three times, exceeding the sector median. The indicative financial risk profile is 'Significant', and the company has limited headroom before breaching the next leverage threshold. While cash flow is substantial, it is insufficient to rapidly reduce debt, leaving the balance sheet sensitive to EBITDA declines.

Looking forward, Amgen's ability to deleverage will depend on revenue growth and margin expansion, which face headwinds from biosimilar competition and pricing pressures. The company's substantial dividend distributions absorb a large portion of free cash flow, limiting debt reduction. Given these factors, we view the credit as stable but with limited upgrade potential unless leverage is meaningfully reduced.

credit_strengths.text: Amgen 的收入基礎龐大且持續增長，年度銷售額超過三百六十億。公司的營業利潤率約為百分之二十五，遠高於醫療保健行業中位數，反映其強大的定價能力和成本控制。此盈利能力支持內部現金生成，並為應對生物相似藥競爭和報銷壓力帶來的利潤率壓力提供緩衝。
營運現金流保持強勁，接近一百億，輕鬆覆蓋資本支出並產生超過八十億的自由現金流。此現金生成支撐公司償還債務、支付股息和投資於其研發管線的能力。持續的現金流亦提供靈活性，以管理即將到期的債務而無需依賴外部融資。

key_risks.text: Amgen 面臨來自政府和商業支付方的重大定價和報銷壓力，如風險因素中所強調。這些壓力可能侵蝕收入和盈利能力，尤其是在生物相似藥競爭加劇的情況下。此外，與 IRS 的持續稅務爭議以及 OECD 最低稅收規則的潛在變化可能導致額外負債，進一步緊張現金流。
債務到期結構顯示大部分債務在五年後到期，但近期到期債務包括未來十二個月內的一筆顯著金額。由於現金餘額僅覆蓋部分這些義務，公司將需要再融資或使用營運現金流。信貸市場的任何中斷可能增加再融資成本或緊張流動性。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率約為三又三分之一倍，低於行業中位數，表明營業收入覆蓋利息支出但緩衝少於同業。此相對緊張的覆蓋率，加上顯著的槓桿，表明債務償還可控但易受盈利下降影響。營業收入下降可能迅速壓力覆蓋率。
自由現金流對債務比率適度低於百分之十五，營運現金流對債務比率亦低於行業標準。這表明內部現金生成雖為正，但不會迅速去槓桿化資產負債表。公司依賴持續現金流償還債務，任何運營挫折可能損害其有機降低槓桿的能力。

overall_credit_view.text: Amgen 的信貸狀況特點是顯著槓桿，淨債務對 EBITDA 高於三倍，超過行業中位數。指示性財務風險狀況為「顯著」，公司在突破下一槓桿閾值前餘地有限。雖然現金流龐大，但不足以迅速減少債務，使資產負債表對 EBITDA 下降敏感。
展望未來，Amgen 的去槓桿能力將取決於收入增長和利潤率擴張，而這些面臨生物相似藥競爭和定價壓力的逆風。公司的大量股息分配吸收大部分自由現金流，限制債務減少。鑑於這些因素，我們認為信貸穩定但除非槓桿顯著降低，否則升級潛力有限。
